channel.title: Eurasia Classic News
channel.description: A review of classical music. Orchestras, concertos, and interviews from Europe and Korea.

item.title: Cellist Dongyeol Lee Makes European Debut at Prague’s Smetana Hall
item.description: Korean cellist Dongyeol Lee performs Dvořák’s Cello Concerto with the North Czech Philharmonic at Smetana Hall, Prague.

item.title: From the Resonance of Tradition to Tchaikovsky: Gunpo Prime Philharmonic Presents Boheoja Resounds
item.description: World premiere by Woojung Choi and harpist Mirjam Schröder highlight the orchestra’s 133rd subscription concert.

item.title: Young Conductors Take the Podium at Haydn Hall: IMK & mdW’s Classical Bridge
item.description: Four young conductors lead the Szolnok Symphony Orchestra at Esterházy Palace, Eisenstadt.

item.title: Sungmin Cho Shares the Stage with Maxim Vengerov at the Beethoven Festival
item.description: The 61st Ludwig van Beethoven Music Festival closes in Teplice with the North Czech Philharmonic.

item.title: Rising Violin Star Charlotte Spruit Performs at the Salzburg Mozarteum with the Sofia Philharmonic
item.description: Mozart's Violin Concerto No. 1 in the composer's birthplace — the Kronberg Academy violinist joins Nayden Todorov and the Sofia Philharmonic.

item.title: First Step Toward the World's Greatest Stage — IMK Scholarship Concert Resonates in the Musikverein's Golden Hall
item.description: The 58th Schwingungen Scholarship Concert brings trombonist Martin Felsberger to Vienna's Musikverein with Tomasi's Trombone Concerto.

item.title: Young Virtuoso from the Manhattan School of Music — Yan Fang Makes His Liszt Hall Debut
item.description: Pianist Yan Fang performs Liszt's Piano Concerto No. 1 at the Franz Liszt Academy with the Hungarian State Symphony Orchestra of Szolnok under Manuel Tévar.

item.title: When Germany Met Korea: Stuttgart Philharmonic's Landmark Korean Debut
item.description: At the Lotte Concert Hall, an all-Beethoven programme with the Triple Concerto and the Fourth Symphony.

item.title: Why the Stuttgart Philharmonic Chose Edwin E.S. Kim for Its Korean Debut
item.description: An all-Beethoven programme, a century-old German sound, and a violinist who plays the Concerto as a question rather than a display.
